newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks sharply lower amid renewed rate fears.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks sharply lower amid renewed rate fears.

text.p: Stocks plunged Friday after strong economic data convinced many investors that Wall Street was facing further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.

The Dow Jones industrial average was down 102.56 points, or 1.57 percent, at 6,437.49 at 1 p.m. EDT. Losers swamped gainers by a 22-to-3 ratio on New York Stock Exchange volume of more than 237 million shares.
"Today's numbers have sort of rekindled the fear that (Fed Chairman Alan) Greenspan will have to act," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray and Co.
The Nasdaq composite index sank 22.58 points, or 1.83 percent, to 1,213.19. The S&P 500 index was off 1.86 percent, falling 14.10 points to 744.24.

Stocks were unnerved by bonds' reaction to the economic data. The bellwether 30-year Treasury bond was off 26/32, or $8.125 on a $1,000 bond, and its yield climbed to 7.18 percent from Thursday's close at 7.11 percent. The bond's price and yield move in opposite directions.

Analysts said stronger-than-expected core March producer price data and an upward revision in February retail sales figures further convinced traders the Fed would boost interest rates at its May 20 policy-making meeting.
Some had harboured hopes that the March 25 Fed rate hike would be all that was needed to keep inflation in check.

"I don't think there's really too many shreds of good news in the data for people who thought that the Fed was going to be 'one-and-done,'" said Charles White, managing director of money management firm Avatar Associates.

The Labour Department said producer prices fell 0.1 percent in March after dropping 0.4 percent in February. But the so-called core rate, excluding volatile food and energy components, rose 0.4 percent vs. a 0.1 percent fall in the previous month.
Economists in a Reuters poll had forecast, on average, the producer price index (PPI) would be unchanged in March. The PPI without the food and energy components was expected to be up 0.1 percent.

Meanwhile, the Commerce Department said retail sales rose 0.2 percent in March compared with a revised 1.5 percent increase in February. Retail sales had been expected to rise 0.6 percent after an original February reading of a 0.8 percent rise.
Technical analysts have said they expect stocks to return to the lows set last week at around 6,400 before any rallies.
Technology stocks again led Wall Street's downdraft.
Traders said investors were jittery ahead of Intel Corp.'s quarterly earnings report Monday and speculation that Intel would make deeper-than-usual price cuts in its Pentium chips.
Intel was off 3-3/4 to 133-1/2, Advanced Micro Devices Inc. fell 1-1/4 to 38-3/8 and Texas Instruments Inc. lost 1-1/8 to 81-1/2.
Boston Scientific Corp. tumbled 14-3/4 to 45-3/4 after the medical device maker said its first-quarter earnings would fall short of analysts' expectations.
Stock in Loehmann's Inc. fell 2-1/4 to 8-5/8 after the retailer said it expected quarterly earnings to fall well below expectations.
